reason: Assessed alert paths: 1) java/xss - user input flows into the LDAP filter string, which is then reflected in HTML output via encodeForHTML, but the XSS occurs because the filter string itself (containing user input) is concatenated into the HTML response without sufficient sanitization; 2) java/ldap-injection - user input directly influences the LDAP filter string used in the search, making it vulnerable to injection. Both alerts are exploitable as the resolved sink values depend on user input.

evidence.note: filter variable contains user input directly
user input flows into HTML output via filter string
